entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_MANUAL_OVERRIDE
entry.description: The pilot has taken the sticks and autonomous commands are being refused. Distinct from simply not being in a guided mode: it means a command was interrupted, which the heartbeat's mode flags cannot express.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_READY_TO_TAKEOFF
entry.description: Pre-flight checks pass and a takeoff command would be accepted.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_HOME_SET
entry.description: The aircraft has recorded a home point.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_LRF_TARGET_VALID
entry.description: The rangefinder target fields hold a real geo-referenced point.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_WAYPOINT_REACHED
entry.description: The aircraft is at the waypoint identified by waypoint_seq. Reported as state rather than only as a command acknowledgement, so a ground station that missed the ack can still see where things stand.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_YAW_REACHED
entry.description: The aircraft is on the heading identified by yaw_seq.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS_FLAG_ALTITUDE_REACHED
entry.description: The aircraft is at the altitude identified by altitude_seq.

enum.name: LYREBIRD_USER_1_SELECTOR
enum.description: param1 selector on MAV_CMD_USER_1 (31010). Lyrebird uses the standard user-command range for payload operations that have no named MAV_CMD, keeping this dialect's own command ids free; the selector tells the aircraft which operation is meant. A ground station that does not know Lyrebird still sees a well-formed user command.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_1_GIMBAL_RELATIVE
entry.description: Nudge the gimbal by a delta: param2 pitch, param3 yaw (degrees).

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_1_RELEASE_MANUAL_OVERRIDE
entry.description: Release the RC manual-override latch and resume autonomous control.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_1_RELEASE_SAFETY
entry.description: Return command authority to the Pilot. Only a frame signed with the Safety Computer's key is honoured; the Pilot cannot release safety. MAVLink counterpart of HTTP /releaseSafetyControl.

enum.name: LYREBIRD_USER_2_SELECTOR
enum.description: param1 selector on MAV_CMD_USER_2 (31011). Payload sensing operations, for the same reason as LYREBIRD_USER_1_SELECTOR.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_2_LRF_MEASURE
entry.description: Fire the laser rangefinder once; the reading surfaces on the telemetry stream.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_2_CAPTURE_TEMPERATURE
entry.description: Read the thermal spot temperature; result_param2 carries hundredths of a degree.

entry.name: LYREBIRD_USER_2_CAPTURE_THERMAL_IMAGE
entry.description: Trip one shutter on the thermal payload, storing thermal R-JPEG plus wide/zoom when enabled.

message.name: LYREBIRD_STATUS
message.description: Lyrebird-specific aircraft state with no standard MAVLink equivalent. Streamed at a low rate alongside the standard telemetry.
message.field: Timestamp since system boot.
Rangefinder target latitude. Valid only with LRF_TARGET_VALID.

Gimbal pitch relative to the aircraft, as DJI reports it. Carried rather than derived: composing the two attitudes MAVLink already sends recovers the right sign and slope but lands about 1.5 degrees out, because DJI's joint angles include a mounting offset that no amount of algebra can recover from the world attitude. Measured over 48 samples of a hand-tilted aircraft.

message.name: LYREBIRD_CONFIG
message.description:
The aircraft's identity and how to reach its other services. Everything here is static for the life of a session, so it is streamed slowly and in its own message rather than weighing down LYREBIRD_STATUS, which carries state that changes.
It exists so a ground station learns what GET /config would have told it without needing the HTTP surface at all. MAVLink streams state rather than answering polls, so the answer to a read arrives on its own rather than on request.
message.field: Port the HTTP command surface listens on.
Port the JSON telemetry stream listens on.
Capabilities of this airframe.
Name this aircraft answers to, as configured in the app.
Address the aircraft is reachable on.
Streaming mode currently configured, such as "whip".

message.name: AUTOSENSING_STATUS
message.description: Whether on-device detection is running, and how many targets it currently holds. Streamed at a low rate so a ground station that joins mid-flight learns the state without asking, and so a viewer can tell "detection is off" from "detection is on and sees nothing".
message.field: Timestamp since system boot.
Detection cycle the target count belongs to.
Confidence below which a detection is discarded.
Non-zero while detection is running.
Targets in the cycle named by frame_id.
Which detector is selected, such as "edge" or "none".

message.name: AUTOSENSING_TARGET
message.description:
One detected object, emitted once per target per detection cycle rather than as a list.
MAVLink messages are fixed-size, so a list would either cap the number of targets or truncate them. Emitting one message each borrows the pattern ADSB_VEHICLE uses for traffic: no cap, and a dropped packet costs one target rather than the whole frame.
target_index and target_count delimit a cycle, so a receiver knows when it has the whole set and can drop anything left over from the previous one. A cycle with nothing in it is reported by AUTOSENSING_STATUS with target_count zero, which is what clears a stale overlay.
The bounding box is normalised to the frame, in the left/top/right/bottom form the detector produces; converting to centre and extent here would only invite the receiver to convert it back.
message.field: Timestamp since system boot.
Detection cycle this target belongs to.
Left edge of the bounding box, 0 to 1.
Top edge of the bounding box, 0 to 1.
Right edge of the bounding box, 0 to 1.
Bottom edge of the bounding box, 0 to 1.
Detector confidence, 0 to 1, or NaN when not reported.
Index of this target within its cycle.
Total targets in this cycle.
Class the detector assigned, such as "PERSON".
